Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

we pronoun

also us, with us, of us

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.14.1: sī vōs valētis, nōs valēmus
Petr. 75.1: nēmō nostrum nōn peccat

nōs, nostrum (nostrī)

pronoun, first person plural: dative and ablative nōbīs

we, us

Left out unless stressed (sī vōs valētis, nōs valēmus). Of the genitives, nostrum is “of us” as part of the group (nēmō nostrum, none of us; utrīusque nostrum, of each of us), nostrī the object of a feeling (nostrī amantius). “With us” is nōbīscum. Writers of letters often say “we” of themselves: haec properantēs scrīpsimus, I wrote this in a hurry.

Examples

  • sī vōs valētis, nōs valēmus

    If you are well, we are well.Cic. Fam. 14.14.1

  • Eāmus; dūc nōs, sōdēs.

    Let’s go; lead us there, please.Ter. Ph. 103

  • nēmō nostrum nōn peccat. hominēs sumus, nōn deī

    None of us doesn’t do wrong. We are human, not gods.Petr. 75.1

  • fuistī here nōbīscum

    You were with us yesterday.Sen. Ep. 64.1

  • domus utrīusque nostrum aedificātur strēnuē

    The houses of both of us are going up apace.Cic. Q. fr. 2.4.2

  • advolā ad nōs eō animō ut nōs amēs, tē amārī sciās. cētera cōram agēmus. haec properantēs scrīpsimus.

    Fly to us, in the spirit of loving us and knowing you are loved. The rest we’ll settle face to face. I wrote this in a hurry.Cic. Att. 4.4.1

See also I, our, ourselves, you.
